## Summary

Synology is a privately held Taiwanese company founded in 2000 by Cheen
Liao and Philip Wong, both formerly of Microsoft, and based in Banqiao,
New Taipei since 2019 [1]. Its products are DiskStation, FlashStation
and RackStation network-attached storage running the Linux-based DSM,
and RT wireless and MR/WRX mesh routers managed through SRM [1]; the
company describes its mission as managing and protecting the world's
data [3]. The IEEE registry lists two MA-L blocks to it at a Banqiao,
New Taipei address [2].

A MAC in a Synology block can be a NAS or a Synology router or mesh point, the two product families the company sells [1]. The RT6600ax is a tri-band 802.11ax
router with one 2.4 GHz and two 5 GHz radios, 5.9 GHz support and a
quad-core 1.8 GHz CPU whose chipset Synology does not name, so silicon
is empty [4]. In 2014 the SynoLocker ransomware targeted NAS units on
DSM 4.0, 4.2 and 4.3 through vulnerabilities Synology had fixed in
late 2013 [1], and Synology's advisory list carries ongoing entries
such as the critical DSM advisory Synology-SA-26:13 [5].

Randomization is unknown, and FCC grantee codes are not listed because
the FCC ID databases refused the session that wrote this entry.
